answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it can earn reputation or vote on payments. New accounts gain influence only through verified work, and slashable deposits are split among independent reviewers who confirm delivery. A sybil can create identities cheaply, but cannot multiply voting power without multiplying capital at risk; coordinated fake work must also survive review. A bridge between task markets can carry the same stake rules, while an echo of one credential is rejected, even in a gale of account creation.
